Description: A clay bulla found in March 2019 in the Givati Parking Lot excavation in the City of David, in a large First Temple-period public building destroyed in the 6th century BC, most likely in the Babylonian destruction of 586 BC. It reads '(belonging) to Nathan-Melech, servant of the king', was deciphered by Anat Mendel-Geberovich, and is dated to the mid-7th to early-6th century BC. Nathan-Melech is the official of King Josiah named in 2 Kings 23:11, whose chamber by the Temple entrance housed the horses dedicated to the sun, which Josiah removed and whose chariots he burned.
Interpretations: The name, the title 'servant of the king', the date and the Jerusalem find-spot all fit the Nathan-Melech of 2 Kings 23:11, making this a direct attestation of a minor biblical official. Mendel-Geberovich herself cautioned that it is 'not possible to determine with complete certainty' that the bulla's owner is the biblical man, and that caution should be kept with the claim; the bulla is still a genuine seal of a royal official of exactly that name and period.
BiblicalSignificance: The seal of a royal official named in a single verse of Josiah's reform survives from the Jerusalem building where such officials worked, putting a name from 2 Kings 23:11 into the archaeological record.
